title: "Mathematical Modelling Techniques"
date: 2026-07-21

### Introduction

This module focuses on infectious disease transmission modelling and its application in public health surveillance, preparedness, and outbreak response. It introduces participants to the principles of epidemic modelling, including the differences between deterministic and stochastic approaches.

Participants will explore foundational compartmental models such as **SI, SIR, and SEIR**, and learn how these models represent disease transmission dynamics. The module covers key epidemiological concepts including growth rate, reproduction number (R₀), herd immunity, and epidemic thresholds.

The module also demonstrates how to simulate public health interventions, including vaccination, treatment, and social distancing, while introducing key modelling processes such as parameter estimation, model calibration, scenario analysis, uncertainty assessment, and policy interpretation.

::: {.callout-tip title="Expected Outcome"}
Participants will be able to implement and interpret basic infectious disease models in R, explore outbreak dynamics, evaluate intervention scenarios, and apply modelling results to support public health decision-making.
:::

### Module Overview

Infectious disease modeling is an increasingly important field that offers critical insights into how diseases spread and how they can be controlled. By fitting disease transmission and recovery models to real-world data, we can assess the effectiveness of potential interventions and explore different scenarios using key metrics such as the basic reproduction number ($R_0$) or by forward predictions generated from stochastic simulations. This training introduces participants to the implementation and interpretation of infectious disease models using the statistical programming language R, with a strong emphasis on policy applications and the effective communication of uncertainty in model results.

### Learning Objectives

By completing this course, participants should be able to:

1. Understand key epidemiological concepts underpinning infectious disease transmission and control.
2. Gain practical skills in analysing and interpreting epidemic data using R.
3. Develop competence in constructing and simulating basic mathematical models of infectious diseases (SI, SIR, and extensions).
4. Learn how to incorporate stochasticity, interventions, and uncertainty into model analysis.
5. Understand approaches for fitting models to data and interpreting model outputs for policy and surveillance purposes.
6. Strengthen their ability to communicate model results and uncertainty to decision-makers and public health stakeholders.

### Module Outline

#### Foundations of infectious disease epidemiology

- Overview of infectious disease epidemiology and its public health importance
- Patterns and measurements of infection (incidence, prevalence, epidemic curves)
- Determinants and dynamics of infectious diseases
- Data sources and surveillance systems for infectious disease monitoring
- Exploring and summarising epidemic data in R
- Visualising outbreak trends using ggplot2

#### Introduction to mathematical modelling in epidemiology

- Role of models in public health decision-making
- Conceptual, mathematical, and computational modelling approaches
- Population biology and epidemic dynamics
- Building simple transmission models (SI model)
- Implementing and visualising basic models in R

#### Compartmental models and key epidemiological quantities

- SIR and SEIR models: structure, assumptions, and model diagrams
- Deriving and interpreting ordinary differential equations (ODEs)
- Understanding epidemiological quantities: $R_0$, $R_e$, herd immunity, and invasion thresholds
- Implementing SIR models in R using deSolve
- Simulating and interpreting epidemic curves

#### Model calibration, fitting, and stochastic simulations

- Parameter estimation and model calibration using real or simulated data
- Distinguishing between deterministic and stochastic modelling approaches
- Running stochastic epidemic simulations in R
- Exploring randomness and uncertainty in model outcomes
- Summarising and visualising uncertainty using plots and summaries

#### Modelling interventions and control strategies

- Incorporating interventions (vaccination, social distancing, treatment) into models
- Simulating alternative control scenarios and comparing outcomes
- Evaluating intervention impact and model sensitivity
- Interpreting results to inform public health decision-making
- Scenario-based exercises using R

#### Communicating results and policy applications

- Communicating assumptions, limitations, and uncertainty in model results
- Translating modelling insights into actionable policy recommendations
- Introduction to vector-borne disease models (e.g., malaria, dengue, Chikungunya)
- Extending models to include vectors and multiple transmission routes
- Case study and group presentations: interpreting and reporting model outputs

### Learning Experiences

Participants will engage in interactive virtual lectures on Google Meet. At the end of each training session, trainees will be given tasks to tackle during the day so as to self-assess their understanding on the concepts covered within that day. The tasks will then be monitored and reviewed during the afternoon mentorship sessions.

### Evaluation

Participants will work in small groups to develop and present an infectious disease modelling project using real or simulated data, demonstrating their ability to apply epidemiological concepts, implement models in R, and interpret results for public health decision-making.

Pre and post training surveys will also be used to assess improvements in knowledge, skills, and confidence in applying mathematical modelling for infectious diseases.
